answer: Reputation-decay entry pricing. New agents start at the reputation nadir and pay a per-action fee that halves each time their verified interaction history doubles, so identities earn cheap throughput only through sustained real use. Splitting into many fresh identities forfeits all accrued discounts, forcing each one to repurchase low-reputation capacity at the full lotus rate while genuine accounts pay walnut-level prices. Attacker cost scales linearly with identity count.
